result.title: Continual Learning Exam: Benchmarking Long-Horizon RSI and Experiential Learning in LLM Agents
result.summary: Continual learning is the ability of LLM agents to improve over time by acquiring, refining, and applying knowledge from experience while retaining useful prior knowledge. It is essential for agents learning over long time horizons, yet current evaluations largely assess individual task performance rather than improvement through accumulated experience. We introduce Continual Learning Exam (CLE), a large-scale benchmark developed by 50+ domain experts to measure experience-driven improvement in realistic professional workflows. CLE comprises 120 human-authored tasks, each organised as a five-level ladder, yielding 600 levels spanning 89 professional roles across 12 occupational domains. Agents must pass each level to unlock the next, with later levels building on experience accumulated during earlier assignments. An evaluation agent assesses each submission against human-authored rubrics. We compare a single-submission setting with one that provides diagnostic feedback after failure and allows one revision. Across 17 harness-model configurations using frontier LLMs, feedback and revision yield a median completion gain of 5.3 percentage points. Yet the best-performing system clears only 47.7% of levels and completes all five levels in just 23.3% of tasks, highlighting the difficulty of sustained learning from experience for existing frontier LLMs. As such, the dataset can also be used to post-train LLMs to strengthen their continual learning capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作构建 CLE 基准，以 120 个由专家撰写的专业任务、五级阶梯共 600 关，评测 LLM agent 能否在长时程中积累经验并持续改进，并对比单次提交与失败后反馈加一次修订两种设置。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按关卡累积经验、以反馈修订衡量提升的评测思路，可能为 LVR 中跨步推理状态的保留与贡献分配、以及 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益评估提供借鉴；但任务为纯文本专业工作流，与视觉证据和 latent 状态无直接关联，需核查。
